name: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma, lymphocyte-depleted type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of Reed-Sternberg cells with a background of markedly depleted lymphocytes
Immunohistochemical positivity for CD30 and CD15 with variable CD20 expression
Painless lymphadenopathy often with systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of Reed-Sternberg cells with lymphocyte depletion and supportive immunophenotyping
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of other lymphoma subtypes and infectious causes is essential

searchTerms: neck lymph node swelling without pain

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of Reed-Sternberg cells on lymph node biopsy
searchTerms: presence of specific abnormal cells in lymph node biopsy
Reed-Sternberg cells found in lymph tissue
diagnostic cells seen in lymph node sample

common.notes: Often intermittent and associated with night sweats

common.symptomName: Unintentional weight loss exceeding 10% body weight
searchTerms: losing significant body weight without trying

common.notes: May be detected on physical exam or imaging

searchTerms: intense itch but no skin changes

occasional.symptomName: Mediastinal mass causing cough or dyspnea
searchTerms: chest mass causing cough or breathing difficulty
mass in chest leading to cough or shortness of breath

occasional.notes: Secondary to bone marrow involvement or chronic disease
searchTerms: symptoms from low red blood cells
fatigue and pale skin due to anemia
bone discomfort that intensifies at night

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to CNS involvement
searchTerms: neurological symptoms from brain or spinal involvement
nerve problems due to central nervous system disease
brain or spinal cord related neurological signs
symptoms caused by cancer affecting immune system

imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Ultrasound or CT of abdomen showing hepatosplenomegaly
genetic: No specific recurrent genetic mutations; complex karyotypes may be present
EBV (Epstein-Barr Virus) association in some cases
other: Histopathology showing classic Reed-Sternberg cells with lymphocyte depletion
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD30 and CD15 markers

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging lymph nodes with systemic symptoms
Unexplained persistent fever and night sweats
Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Hodgkin Lymphoma, Version 2.2024.
Orphanet: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma, lymphocyte-depleted type (ORPHA:98846).
